date_note: Day E-Money posted its notice on the X1 homepage, per Daily Security; the company learned of the leak on Nov 20.
title: E-Money's X1 investment platform says customer data may have leaked after expert-account misuse
summary: Daily Security reports that E-Money, a Daou Kiwoom Group affiliate, posted a notice on Nov 24 about a possible personal-data leak at its X1 stock-information service. The company learned of it on Nov 20 through refund-impersonation contacts and found signs of expert-account misuse and server file access. The scale and the date of first intrusion are under investigation.
plain: A Korean stock-information service says customer data such as names, phone numbers and payment details may have leaked, and customers got fake refund contacts. The size of the leak is still being checked.
exec: The company says it has not confirmed any effect on Kiwoom Securities or other group affiliates, per Daily Security.
action: E-Money advises customers not to respond to refund or compensation messages or click their links, and to change passwords reused on other sites.

validation.note: Only Daily Security read, relaying E-Money's own notice; the notice itself was not opened.
